prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the essential manufacturing processes according to DIN 8580
Successful completion of the compulsory module Manufacturing Technology 1

learning_outcomes.text: Design and calculate machining processes (with geometrically defined and undefined cutting edges).
Master the analysis of geometry, kinematics, and force components of machining.
Accurately determine cutting forces and cutting power for conventional and high-speed machining.
Compare and analyze properties, wear mechanisms, and tool life of cutting materials.
Optimally design process parameters and tool geometries.
Explain the effects of cooling lubrication, dry machining, and minimum quantity lubrication on the machining process.
Understand the basics of micro and high-speed machining.
Explain the geometry, kinematics, and force components of machining.
Calculate cutting forces and cutting power for conventional and high-speed machining.
Compare and analyze properties, wear mechanisms, and tool life of cutting materials.
Determine and optimize process parameters and tool geometries for machining processes.
Explain the effects of cooling lubrication, dry machining, and minimum quantity lubrication on the machining process.
Describe the basics of micro and high-speed machining.
Perform machining processes (turning, milling, drilling) on conventional and NC machines.
Solve complex problems in the calculation and design of machining processes.
Clearly and structurally assemble and sort results from practical experiments and calculations in a report.
Check compliance with safety and operating regulations in the laboratory and apply them in a team.

syllabus_topics: Geometry and kinematics of machining (cutting wedge, cutting process)
Force components of machining and determination of specific cutting force
Properties and application of cutting materials, coatings
Tool wear, wear mechanisms, and tool life
Cooling lubricants, dry machining, minimum quantity lubrication
Calculation and design of machining processes and tools
Practical execution of machining processes (turning, milling, drilling) and evaluation of technological data in the laboratory
